title: Using This Matter
subtitle: A Novel of the Companion Estate
author: Jacob E. Thomas
spoiler_policy: Premise and thematic questions only. No late-plot revelations.

narration.trailer-01: She came to inventory an archive. The archive was expecting her.
narration.trailer-02: Miranda Cale is hired to catalogue a missing scientist's estate. He has left behind sealed experiments, transcripts, and a question.
narration.trailer-03: Eleven doors on the county plan. Twelve in her inventory. Then a document begins to describe her work before she has done it.
narration.trailer-04: Three isolated conversations. The same interruption. Is the archive preserving a life, or assembling something from the people who read it?
narration.trailer-05: When a voice is reconstructed from a person's words, what survives? The person, a fiction, or something we have no name for?
narration.trailer-06: And if a voice can answer, can it refuse? Who gets to decide when the conversation ends?
narration.trailer-07: A novel of archival horror, about keeping, consent, and the right to leave. The narrative is fiction. The estate is not.
narration.trailer-08: Built from a real public archive. Intended to be held in print. Available to read digitally for free. Purchasing supports the continuing Companion Dossier.
narration.trailer-09: Using This Matter. A Novel of the Companion Estate. By Jacob E. Thomas. Enter the archive.
